messages.Text:
The conversation so far:
Developer: how do I get the X-token after a mobile OTP login
You: Call /abha/api/v3/profile/login/verify/user with the chosen ABHANumber, the txnId and the verify token in the T-token header. The response carries token, which is the X-token, with expiresIn and refreshToken.

The developer's new message:
and when it expires? do they have to login again

spec.description:
**Endpoint:** `GET /abha/api/v3/profile/account/request/token`

**Flow:** **Access Tokens & Encryption** - independent API; call the one that fits your identifier / modality.

---

This API endpoint is used to request a token for accessing a user’s ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) profile. This token is essential for authenticating and authorizing the user to perform various actions within their profile.

parameters.description: Current UTC timestamp in ISO-8601 format.
parameters.name: TIMESTAMP

200.description: The token was successfully generated and sent to the user’s registered contact method.

400.description: The 400 response code indicates a bad request

value.description: Invalid Credentials. Make sure your API invocation call has a header: 'Authorization : Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN' or 'Authorization : Basic ACCESS_TOKEN' or 'apikey: API_KEY'

reply.Text:
No, they don't need to login again. The response includes a **refreshToken** alongside the X-token.

When the X-token expires (after `expiresIn` seconds, typically 1800 seconds / 30 minutes), call **`GET /abha/api/v3/profile/account/request/token`** with the `refreshToken` in the `R-token` header to get a fresh X-token without requiring re-login.

The refreshToken itself lasts longer—`refreshExpiresIn` (typically 1,296,000 seconds / 15 days). Only when *that* expires do they need to login again.

See the [Refresh user token endpoint](https://abdm.gov.in/docs/hiecm/v3/api/m1/endpoints/m1-get-v3-profile-account-request-token) in the portal.
